items.author: fregie
items.descZh: Tokenhush 是一款针对 AI 编码工具的本地安全网关，旨在防止敏感数据在传输过程中泄露，背景是 AI 辅助开发工具普及带来的隐私风险。其核心功能是作为本地回环 HTTP 网关，在数据离开机器前自动检测并脱敏秘密和个人身份信息，通过替换为占位符实现保护。亮点包括无需中间人攻击或根证书，确保安全无侵入，同时能高效处理多个文件中的秘密检测，每个值都被替换。适用场景主要是开发者在使用 AI 编码工具时，保护代码库中的 API 密钥、密码等敏感信息，适用于需要本地安全控制的团队或个人项目。
items.quote: 本地、可逆的密钥脱敏，专为 AI 编码工具设计。无中间人攻击，无根证书。
items.titleZh: Show HN：Tokenhush – 将您的秘密信息排除在 Claude Code 发送内容之外。

items.title: Show HN: Built-in APM for vibe-coded apps so your AI can fix them
items.desc: description: Every app on Croft now comes with monitoring built in response time tracking, error grouping, logs, alerts, and MCP tools so your assistant can fix what breaks. title: Monitoring for every Croft app, with nothing to install image: https://oncroft.net/assets/og/blog/monitoringbuiltinforeverycroftapp.jpg?v=1790208243 [Skip to content](main) Every app on Croft now comes with monitoring built in. No SDK, no agent, no dashboards to set up, no extra cost. When something breaks you get an email and your AI assistant can see the error, fix it, and deploy the fix. The problem we are solving You built an app by talking to Claude or ChatGPT. It worked, you shared it with your team, and now it is part of how the business runs. Then it breaks. Your team sees “something went wrong.” Your assistant sees nothing at all. Traditional APM New Relic, Datadog, Sentry needs an account, an SDK wired into the code, and usually an engineer to set it up and read the results. That does not fit someone who built an app in an afternoon by conversation. What you get Starting today, every app on Croft includes monitoring. Your app runs; Croft records what matters: Response time breakdown \ for apps on the Croft runtime, see where time goes with a stacked breakdown of database, external API calls, and code execution (the same New Relicstyle profiling, built in). Throughput and failure rate \ track ok, rejected, and failed requests over time, with charts showing patterns and spikes. Error groups \ Croft autogroups errors by type and location. The same error from a hundred requests shows as one group, with a stack trace and which requests failed. Slow requests \ waterfall views of your slowest requests, showing exactly which database queries or API calls took the time. Slowest SQL \ a list of your slowest database queries, so you know what to optimise. 7 days of logs \ search by level, time, or keywords, right in the panel. Health checks and resources \ track your app’s health check, server CPU, memory, and database size over time. Deploy markers \ charts show when each deploy shipped, so you can see exactly when a change went out. All up to the minute, all included. Response time stacked by database, external, and code with deploy markers The fix loop When an app breaks, your AI assistant can help. The Croft MCP includes three monitoring tools: app\_errors \ list open error groups, read stack traces, and see which requests failed. app\_metrics \ fetch response time, throughput, failure rate, or server resources for any app. logs \ search and read the last 7 days of logs, filtered by level or keywords. Your assistant can read the error via MCP, see the logs and stack trace, fix the code it wrote, and deploy the fix usually before you have made tea. Or click Fix with Build on any error in the panel, and it hands the stack trace and logs to Croft Build the builtin AI chat which fixes and redeploys. When you ship a fix, error groups autoresolve after Croft sees no new occurrences in the next deploy. No manual triage, no stale open errors cluttering the list. Throughput split by ok, rejected, and failed requests Alerts you can live with Croft sends alert emails for three things: New error \ the first time Croft sees an error it has not grouped before, with the stack trace and a Fix with Build link. High failure rate \ when a large percentage of requests fail over a short window, you get one alert with the failure count and Fix with Build (not one per request). App unhealthy \ if your app’s health check fails or the app stops responding, with a confirmation email when it recovers. Once per app per day at most, so you are informed but not flooded. Privacy: data stays on your server Logs, errors, stack traces, and slow request traces live on your own Croft server, with 7day retention. Only aggregate counts and timings requests per second, average response time, failure rate go to the control plane for charts. No query strings, request bodies, cookies, or IP addresses are recorded. Your telemetry is yours. Included. No extra cost. Monitoring is included on Solo and Team plans, with no usage pricing or separate bill. Your apps come with monitoring the day you deploy them. [See what monitoring gives you →](/monitoring/) The vibecoded app lifecycle You build an app in an afternoon by chatting with AI. It runs on your own private server, behind one login. Your team uses it, it becomes part of how the business works and now, when it breaks, you know. Your assistant knows. And the fix ships before anyone has to ask. That is the point: the speed of building with AI, on a foundation a real business can keep. Monitoring is the latest piece. More to come. [More from the blog](/blog/) Stake out your croft. Your team's first app could be live before lunch. [Get your croft](https://app.oncroft.net/signup) 7 days free, no card to start. items.author: richchetwynd
items.descZh: 针对AI对话快速构建的应用在团队使用中易发生故障且传统APM工具配置复杂的问题，Croft平台推出了无需安装SDK或代理的内置监控方案。该方案核心功能涵盖响应时间堆叠分解（数据库、外部API及代码执行）、吞吐量与失败率追踪、自动分组错误、慢请求瀑布图、慢SQL列表以及7天日志检索。其最大亮点是集成了AI修复闭环，通过MCP工具AI助手可直接读取错误堆栈并自动修复部署，且错误组在无新发生后自动解析。告警机制针对新错误、高失败率和应用不健康发送邮件，每日每应用最多限制一次以防骚扰。数据隐私方面，详细日志和追踪数据仅存于用户自有服务器，控制平面仅接收聚合指标。此功能完全免费包含在Solo和Team套餐中，专为需要企业级稳定保障的AI构建应用（vibecoded apps）设计。
items.quote: 当有东西出错时，你会收到一封邮件，你的 AI 助手就能看到错误、修复它并部署修复。

items.descZh: 这个工具是一个基于 Rust 和 ratatui 构建的终端用户界面，用于运行和监控多个 socat 中继。它将 socat 的多路中继管理功能与类任务管理器的交互体验结合在一起，方便在同一个终端窗口中集中控制。亮点在于利用 Rust 的内存安全和并发能力，结合 ratatui 的响应式 UI 框架，实现了中继状态的实时刷新和稳定运行。适用于需要在本地或远程服务器上维护多个网络端口转发或数据桥接任务的运维和开发场景。

[package.json](/ifoster01/jeveffort/blob/main/package.json "package.json") View all files Repository files navigation jeveffort Does letting Jev choose Claude Code's reasoning effort, step by step, save money? At higheffort, barely: about 1%. At max effort, it cut the cost of a coding benchmark by 55% with every test still passing. In a long real session at max, the estimated saving was 4–9%, because rereading the conversation's context is most of the bill. Changing effort on every step never reset the prompt cache. A research project. The code works and the results are reproducible. Unofficial; not affiliated with Anthropic or TypeSafe. Summary [Jev](https://openrouter.ai/typesafe/jev1.13) is TypeSafe's small, cheap decision model. After [AstraAres](https://github.com/miuuyy/AstraAres) used it to choose GPT6 Astra's reasoning effort per step in Codex, several tools appeared doing the same for Claude. The pitch: most agent steps are routine, so run them at low effort and keep deep reasoning for the hard ones. I built a proxy that does this for Claude Code without breaking the prompt cache, confirmed it works, then measured what it saves. Test Result Benchmark at high (24 sessions, hidden tests) Cost −1.1%, thinking −46%, every test passed in both arms Benchmark at max (24 sessions, hidden tests) Cost −55% (−21% without its one outlier task), thinking −98.5%, wall time −58%, every test passed in both arms Real session at max, shadow mode (470 steps, 92 min) Estimated saving 4–9%. Cached context was 82% of spend, thinking 9.5% Effort changes how much the model thinks, and the saving follows thinking's share of the bill. At high, Claude Opus 5.5 thinks little on routine steps, so there's little to cut. At max, it thinks a lot even on routine steps, and Jev moves those down. But in a long session every step rereads hundreds of thousands of tokens of context, which effort doesn't touch. Changing effort doesn't reset the cache Claude Code caches the conversation so each step only pays full price for what's new. Changing effort midsession used to throw that cache away. It no longer has to: Anthropic's [permessage effort](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/buildwithclaude/effortchangeeffortmidconversationbeta)beta lets an effortonly system message change the level while leaving the cached prefix intact. It held inside Claude Code. In the 470step session with effort chosen on every step: 0 unexpected cache misses in 411 checked steps, and a 99.1% cache hit rate. With effort alternating low/high on every step of a test task, each request read the whole previous prefix from cache (26,992 → 34,285 → 35,017 → 35,270 → 35,617 tokens). items.author: ifoster41901
items.descZh: jeveffort 是一款非官方的 Claude Code 扩展，利用 TypeSafe 的小型决策模型 Jev 逐动态调整推理强度，旨在将常规步骤的推理成本降至最低，仅在复杂任务时启用深度思考。其核心技术亮点在于通过 Anthropic 的 per-message effort 机制，在不破坏 prompt 缓存的前提下实现推理强度的动态切换，解决了以往切换强度会导致缓存失效的痛点。实测数据表明，该工具在最大推理强度的基准测试中成功将成本降低了 55%，思考 token 减少了 98.5%，且所有测试依然全部通过；在真实的 470 步长会话中，缓存命中率保持在 99.1%，无意外缓存丢失。这表明该方案非常适合混合了大量常规代码编写与偶尔复杂调试的长周期 AI 编程场景，能够在不牺牲代码质量的前提下显著降低 API 调用成本。
items.quote: 尽最大努力，它将编码基准测试的成本降低了55%，同时所有测试均通过。

[]() [](https://search.maven.org/artifact/io.github.chaosvy/chaostree) [](https://github.com/Chaosvy/ChaosTree/releases) [](/Chaosvy/ChaosTree/blob/main/LICENSE) [](https://github.com/Chaosvy/ChaosTree/actions) [](https://codecov.io/gh/Chaosvy/ChaosTree) _ChaosTree is a zerodependency Java library featuring AVL Trees, RedBlack Trees, BTrees, and B+ Trees._ _Fully compliant with JDK 21 SequencedCollection_ [Documentation Hub](https://chaosvy.github.io/ChaosTree/index.html) • [Benchmarks](benchmarkhighlights) • [Getting Started](gettingstarted) Why ChaosTree Cachelocality first Nary nodes pack into preallocated, exactcapacity arrays — up to \~40% fewer memory stalls on large range scans vs. pointerchasing structures. O(N) bulk loading buildFromSorted and importFlatMatrix construct trees directly from sorted data, with a tunable fill factor \[0.5, 1.0\]. Strictly compatible Built on JDK 21 SequencedCollection / SequencedSet / SequencedMap. Validated against 214,000+ Guava Testlib cases for exact TreeMap/TreeSet semantics. Serializable & Cloneable Native O(N) bulkload restoration on deserialize; full Cloneable support. Zero dependencies Nothing else on the classpath. Getting Started Maven <dependency <groupIdio.github.chaosvy</groupId <artifactIdchaostree</artifactId <version2.0.1</version </dependency Gradle (Kotlin DSL) implementation("io.github.chaosvy:chaostree:2.0.1") Quick Start import chaos.tree.naryMap.BPlusTreeMap; import java.util.NavigableMap; public class Main { public static void main(String[] args) { // Degree64 B+Tree, backed by a contiguous leaflinked list NavigableMap<Integer, String map = new BPlusTreeMap<(); map.put(1, "Chaos"); map.put(2, "Tree"); map.put(3, "Performance"); // Range scans walk the linked leaf layer directly — no tree descent NavigableMap<Integer, String subMap = map.subMap(1, true, 3, true); System.out.println(subMap); } } addFirst() / addLast() are unsupported and failfast — these are strictly sorted structures. Architecture Two engines, chosen by workload: Nary family (BTree, BPlusTree) — maximum read throughput and largescale range scans, zero GC churn. BPlusTree pushes all data into a contiguous doublylinked (SoA) leaf layer for fast sequential reads. Binary family (AVL, RBT) — fast point queries and everyday storage where Nary's extreme cache optimization isn't needed. Deep dives: [Architecture Decision Records](https://chaosvy.github.io/ChaosTree/utils/ADR.html) · [Nary Tree Architecture](https://chaosvy.git
items.author: chaos_vy
items.descZh: ChaosTree 是一款零依赖、高性能的 Java 排序集合库，核心提供二叉树（AVL、红黑树）与 N 叉树（B 树、B+ 树）家族，全面兼容 JDK 21 SequencedCollection 规范。它实现了高度优化的 NavigableMap 和 NavigableSet，支持 O(N) 批量加载、可调填充因子，并提供原生的序列化与克隆支持。其最大亮点在于极致的缓存感知能力，通过将 N 叉节点打包至预分配的精确容量数组，在大规模范围扫描中可减少约 40% 的内存停顿，而 B+ 树更可通过连续叶子链表实现无树下降的快速顺序遍历。该库经过超过 214,000 个 Guava 测试用例的严格验证，确保与标准 TreeMap/TreeSet 语义完全一致，且类路径零污染。它适用于需要极致读取吞吐量、大规模数据范围扫描，同时对内存延迟和 GC 压力有严苛要求的 Java 高性能系统。
items.quote: 树节点被打包进预分配的、容量精确的数组中——与需要追踪指针链的数据结构相比，在大规模范围扫描时，内存停顿减少了约 40%。
